clue.text: Write notes for limited costume design augmented by special ties

indicators.note: a costume design is a fresh arrangement, so the clipped word's letters are rearranged along with the rest
a limited word is held short, so the clue word costume loses its final letter
special here suggests something made up afresh, so the letters of ties are mixed in too

explanation.surface: A costume designer's outfit is enhanced by some fancy neckwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited' trims costume to COSTUM; 'special' and 'design' scramble TIES and COSTUM together; 'augmented by' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: To compose music for words is to provide the notes that accompany a text, as a composer does.

clue.text: Buff will pick up Spooner's cost to employer

indicators.note: to pick up is to hear, signalling the swap is made by sound rather than spelling
the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the starts of the two words trade places

parts.note: buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour, another word for beige
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fan of the deceased will learn what an employer pays out.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BEIGE WILL gives something close to the answer in sound; the swap is approximate, as Spoonerisms often are.
explanation.definitionFit: The total paid in salaries is a major outlay for any business that takes on staff.

clue.text: See 17
Paid for pasture

definitions.meaning: someone who has been paid a fee is, jocularly
grass on which livestock graze serves as fodder for them

explanation.definitionFit: Paying a professional is giving a fee; pasture is grazing that serves as fodder for animals.

clue.text: Insure sign?

definitions.meaning: to guarantee against loss, as an insurer does
playfully, to sign is to write your name under a document

explanation.definitionFit: Insurers guarantee risks, and a signature literally goes beneath the text, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Porter, maybe, one carrying wife's disease

indicators.note: something carrying another holds it inside, so the drink and the numeral enclose the next piece

parts.note: porter is a dark ale, an example of beer
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a wife is jokingly a rib; the 's is just 'is'
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A railway porter is lugging his wife's illness about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' looks like a railway worker, but it is the drink. A rib is a jocular word for a wife, from the Genesis story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical illness caused by lack of thiamine, a vitamin B1 deficiency.

clue.text: So spell the end of lead-free gas

indicators.note: to spell out the final pair of letters is to say one, a word for so, then the other, so the synonym sits between them
the end of the clue word lead-free is its last two letters, a pair of Es

parts.note: so, as in 'and so', means then

explanation.surface: This is how you'd describe the end of petrol containing lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'lead-free' is EE; spelling that out is saying 'E then E', and 'So' gives THEN. Enigmatist's trick hides the mechanism in plain words.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called ethylene, this is a flammable hydrocarbon that exists as a vapour at room temperature.

clue.text: Dairy product, in a nutshell, from which to swat fly

indicators.note: swatting a fly gets rid of it, so the insect's name is knocked out of the longer word

parts.note: in a nutshell means put concisely, or briefly
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheese, in short, from which you must drive off insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like an insect pest on cheese, but it is the very letters removed from BRIEFLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft French cheese made from cow's milk, so a product of the dairy.

clue.text: Energy shown by report of Tellytubby writer in battle scene

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: a report is a spoken account, so the name is given by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Laa-Laa is one of the four Teletubbies in the BBC children's TV show
the writer of the clue refers to himself as me
taken as written

explanation.surface: An energetic report by a children's TV writer about a war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: Laa-Laa is the yellow Teletubby; her name said aloud gives LALA. 'shown by' simply links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This Egyptian place was the site of a decisive Second World War desert campaign in 1942.

clue.text: Undertaking to take possession by force

parts.note: in law, to enter land is to take possession of it
to prise is to force open, as with a lever

explanation.surface: A bold venture of seizing property by violence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link. ENTERPRISE is also Captain Kirk's starship, tying in with 17.
explanation.definitionFit: A venture or project is something undertaken, especially a bold one.

clue.text: Choppers cut

parts.note: choppers is slang for teeth, and babies are said to cut them as they come through the gum

explanation.definitionFit: A baby's first teeth breaking through the gums is described by this verb, so its choppers have come through.

clue.text: The first of Enigmatist's loathsome solvers give him this?

definitions.text: The first of Enigmatist's loathsome solvers give him this?

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the setter's name is used

parts.note: loathsome means vile
the solvers are addressed as ye, an old form of you

explanation.surface: Solvers resentful of a hard setter shoot him a malevolent look.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: E, VILE and YE in sequence give the malicious glare frustrated solvers might aim at Enigmatist.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent stare, believed in folklore to cause harm, which a resentful solver might direct at a setter.

clue.text: Supply items not on the starter menu?

definitions.meaning: the water, gas or electricity piped or wired into homes

definitions.text: items not on the starter menu?
definitions.meaning: main courses, the dishes that follow the starters

explanation.definitionFit: Utilities reach homes through a supply network, and main courses come after the starters on a menu.

clue.text: See 17
See 17
A little pretence and no mistake

indicators.note: a mistake garbles things, so the letters of the preceding words are put in the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A slight bit of faking, and make no error about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' reads as part of the phrase 'and no mistake', but it is the anagram signal; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One hundredth of anything is a tiny share, so a small amount.

clue.text: Spaced-out agent of operations?

parts.note: a verb form with 'to', such as 'to go', names an action; when an adverb comes between its parts it is spaced out

explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical construction in which a word separates 'to' from its verb, as in 'to boldly go'.

clue.text: Mission of "Virgin Soldiers" or 10 21, with famous 16?

definitions.text: Mission of "Virgin Soldiers" or 10 21, with famous 16?

parts.words: Mission of "Virgin Soldiers" or 10 21, with famous 16?
parts.note: the opening words of the Star Trek title sequence, the starship's stated mission, famous for putting an adverb between 'to' and its verb; inexperienced soldiers would have a similar ambition

explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans 17, 14 across, 3 and 14 down. It refers to the starship Enterprise (10 21) and the split infinitive (16); The Virgin Soldiers is a novel about raw National Service recruits.
explanation.definitionFit: This line from the Star Trek opening states the starship's five-year mission of exploration into the unknown.

clue.text: Green measure of what sounds like a see-saw?

definitions.meaning: Ireland is the Emerald Isle, so green suggests Irish, and a measure is a dance
the Irish Sea sounds like an Irish 'see', and a jig is a saw as in jigsaw

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link. The second reading is a playful construction: Irish 'see' plus jig-'saw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively traditional dance from Ireland, a country associated with the colour green.

clue.text: Arm wrapped in wire could be scaled

indicators.note: the limb is wrapped inside the cable, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: a cable is a thick wire
an arm is a limb

explanation.surface: A limb tangled in wire might be climbed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be scaled can be climbed or ascended.

clue.text: I'll achieve excitement — should such an eventuality arise

parts.note: the pronoun I, whose 'will' links to achieving the next piece
a fever is a state of excitement, as in fever pitch

explanation.surface: Someone vows to reach a pitch of thrill, should the chance come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'achieve' is a link: I gets FEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase introduces a hypothetical, meaning on the occasion that something occurs.

clue.text: See 10
Fence whiter today than yesterday

definitions.meaning: a fence made of pointed stakes
becoming lighter in colour, growing pale

explanation.definitionFit: A fence of stakes is a picket; losing colour over time is going white or ashen.

clue.text: Magic formula for tax shift?

definitions.meaning: an incantation (a ... or about a levy (a ...)

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: a spell is a magic formula and a duty is a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker's shift is a period spent on the job, a turn at work.

clue.text: Group that dares to win hospital frame

parts.note: the SAS, the British Special Air Service, has the motto 'Who Dares Wins'
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Elite soldiers storm a hospital window frame.
explanation.walkthrough: The SAS is a British army special forces regiment, known by its motto 'Who Dares Wins'.
explanation.definitionFit: A window frame holding glass panes, as in a sliding sash window.

clue.text: Derek's loud local description of Trig's from the Oracle?

parts.note: Del is short for Derek, as in Del Boy, Derek Trotter of the BBC sitcom Only Fools and Horses

indicators.note: loud here means said out loud, so the word is given by its sound

parts.note: Trigger (Trig) is the dim road sweeper in Only Fools and Horses, and Del would call him 'fick', cockney for thick

explanation.surface: A sitcom character's loud comment about his slow friend sounds oracular.
explanation.walkthrough: In Del's London accent, 'thick' comes out as 'fick', spelt here PHIC. Only Fools and Horses is a classic British TV comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the ancient Greek oracle at Delphi, hence cryptic or ambiguous.

clue.text: See 22 across
VIP's heaving

definitions.meaning: a fashionable or important person, a toff
the rising and falling motion of the sea

explanation.definitionFit: An important socialite is old-fashioned slang for a toff, and the rolling of waves is a swell.

clue.text: Nuts enter into custody

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: Keeping something or someone in your possession or detention, holding on to it.
